name: Farmer
description: Though not educated, <name> was wise. [He/She] knew when to plant to avoid a frost, and could coax oxen to plough a perfect furrow. Life was hard but Nature was bountiful. <name> had much to be thankful for.

name: Swineherd
description: Wandering the forest with rooting hogs for company, carrying a stout stick for beating down acorns and interlopers...this was all <name> knew. Whiling away the hours, chewing mushrooms, alone with [his/her] imagination. Other people's jobs were more onerous, <name> believed.

name: Marshal
description: A wanderer from Barcelona, <name> had the gift of healing animals, and occasionally humans at a pinch. [He/She] was learned, understanding the Moorish faith, and the teachings of Galen and Aristotle. <name> had an excellent sense of humour!

name: Cottar
description: With a field to plough and a cottage to live in, <name> laboured hard. [He/She] had mainly worried about death and taxes. With a dozen destitute dependents, <name> had feared paying out all [his/her] livestock in heriots to the Lord if any died.

name: Gardener
description: <name> had found peace within the wattle fences of the garden, filled with scented flowers and herbs. [He/She] knew their properties well, as food and medicine. Time stood still under the trellises, and <name> would bathe in the scent of new growth.

name: Reeve
description: Rising from humble serf to Reeve offered <name> a coveted place at [his/her] lord's table. Yet overseeing [his/her] fellow labourers was a thankless task. With so much to manage, why not take a little for oneself? <name> certainly felt justified.

name: Herbalist
description: Having once seen a copy of De Materia Medica at Oxford, <name> became a lifelong devotee Dioscorides. Blending this with the teachings of [his/her] mentor, an elderly nun and plantswoman, <name> felt confident in pronouncing upon botanical matters.

name: Roofer
description: <name> felt that [his/her] dizzying head for heights was a divine gift, to be used in architectural celebration of Our Lord. Working among the angels on the great spire of Salisbury Cathedral was the pinnacle of [his/her] career.

name: Bowyer
description: It was said that <name> annihilated 23 French warriors at L’Ecluse, each dispatched with a single, mercifully accurate shot. [His/Her] fame as an archer was only surpassed by <name>’s skill with yew, building fine longbows. They were greatly prized.

name: Carpenter
description: <name> was a member of the Brotherhood of Carpenters, a guild that offered heavenly rewards. To work all day with wood, knowing that in death the Brotherhood would pay for burial and even have prayers said at the chantry made <name> deeply thankful.

name: Wheelwright
description: <name> of <origin> believed there were many spokes in the wheel of life. [He/She] enjoyed lending a hand with repairs and building projects, even fashioning a crucifix at the behest of a group of mummers for their mystery play.

name: Builder
description: From sawn timber lintel frames to trampled cob for thick, curved walls, <name> could work them with [his/her] strong, raw hands. <name> was known to be rough and ready, just as quick to anger as to lauch into bawdy tales or raucous songs.

name: Brick maker
description: <name> loved the slippery feeling of earth between [his/her] toes. [He/She] spent a happy childhood plugging weathered clay in the yards of Hull, forming an array of ruddy blocks destined for castles and fortresses. [He/She] was an absolute brick.

name: Shipwright
description: <name> had done [his/her] time building vessels on the docks, and could turn [his/her] calloused hand to all manner of construction. Ports being rough and ready places, <name> also knew how to throw a punch and dodge a scoundrel's shiv.

name: Innkeep
description: <name> was known for the crustiest pie pastry in <origin>, and poured a generous pitcher of ale to boot. Jovial and fair, [he/she] never hesitated to knock a few thick heads together if fights broke out, either.

name: Butcher
description: <name> knew animals inside out, as befits a member of the Butcher's Guild. [He/She] had a gentle way with all beasts, and dealt their fate swiftly. <name> knows how to prepare exotic cuts fit for a king, which peasants have never tasted.

name: Chef
description: Once an enfant de cuisine under the great master Taillevent, <name> became chef to the great houses of England. Despite [his/her] snobbery, there's no denying <name>'s culinary expertise regarding all manner of edible flora, fauna, and fungi.

name: Brewster
description: You could tell <name>'s profession by [his/her] tall black hat and broomstick. Yes, [he/she] brewed ale. <name> was a grafter, and resented the Abbot's assumption that [he/she] used [his/her] wiles to get pious men drunk. You can't hold back an entrepreneur.

name: Architect
description: If truth be told, <name> was jealous of Henry Yeverley. Although [he/she] could never rival the Master Mason of the King's Works, <name> thought [his/her] advanced ideas on architecture, acquired at the Château de Vincennes, worthy of greater renown.

name: Master builder
description: <name> loved getting stuck into a complex project. [He/She] spent many years crossing Europe in search of instruction. <name> understood how to create gravity-defying structures with stone and iron, taught by the nameless, genius cathedral builders.

name: Engineer
description: <name> took pride in the vast engines of war [he/she] designed. <name> dreamed of one day creating a device as legendary as the great Warwolf trebuchet created by Master James of St. George. How the tarbarrels and corpses would fly!

name: Scribe
description: The pen is mightier than the sword, and <name> had certainly reveled in a little power. Called upon to wield [his/her] quill by merchants and gentry, <name> recorded their contracts, their laws and their deaths in littera antiqua, with a flourish.

name: Monk
description: <name> liked to potter in the still room, with [his/her] salves and potions. Those brought to the hospital were truly at the mercy of God. But <name> liked to offer what little curative help [he/she] could to ease their suffering.

name: Hunter
description: They said in <origin> that <name> was born with a bow in [his/her] hand. In the warmer months, <name> would hunt wolves, [his/her] tongue lolling and eyes bright as [he/she] loped through the forest, lithe, invisible, and poised to strike.

name: Archer
description: From being fostered as a squire through to becoming a mounted archer, <name> was a true career soldier. Scarred and surly, [he/she] had kept a cool head at Saint-Omer and Morlaix, escaping without victory but with [his/her] life.

name: Recruit
description: <name> practiced when [he/she] could with the longbow, but ploughing and reaping duties generally took precedence. No matter, <name> was enlisted to fight in France, ending at the Siege of Tournai. A string to [his/her] bow and a tale for the fireside.

name: Healer
description: A cloistered life, tending the abbey gardens and copying fine manuscripts, spun <name> along a golden thread of erudition. Alas, the pitiless Abbott urged [him/her] to go forth and heal the sick and the poor. So, reluctantly, <name>’s exile began.

name: Field doctor
description: By day, <name> tended fallen troops. But at night, the rank threat of battlefield dysentery and marsh fever invaded [his/her] sleep. Bad air from bloated corpses was the stuff of nightmares. Of the four horsemen, <name> dreaded pestilence most.

name: Nun
description: <name>'s family paid the church her dowry, granting her a pious and cloistered life. Instead, a small, persistent voice bid her roam over battlefields, stitching up wounds and praying with the broken as they gasped their last. It was <name>'s calling.

name: Knight
description: Chivalry was <name>'s lifeblood, and [he/she] would die for honour. A knight of St John, <name> had become a warrior monk, defended Rhodes from infidels. Loyalty, justice and generosity were [his/her] watchwords, but woe betide the summa culpabilis.

name: Soldier
description: <name> had seen gruesome battles, weak leaders and fearsome foes. Expecting to face death in France, <name> trained constantly and was fighting fit, belligerent and always guarded. We often give our enemies the means of our own destruction.

name: Army cook
description: An army marches on its stomach, and <name> knew how to keep the campfires burning and soldier's bellies full. [His/Her] meals weren't exactly gourmet but <name> was a keen butcher, and could fillet the opposition pretty skillfuly in retreat.

name: Mercenary
description: <name> had roamed Italy causing the worst kinds of trouble with the Company of St George, a group of freemen whose goal was pillaging and chaos. All good things must end, and <name> had subsequently dug ditches and escaped hanging for petty thievery.

name: Farrier
description: <name> is a horse whisperer. [He/She] keeps equine hooves healthy and shod in iron. It doesn't pay much, but it's a stable job.

name: Lorimer
description: <name> has furrows of concentration etched on [his/her] brow, and brawny arms from working hammer and bellows. Whether a humble horse bit or a knight's spurs, <name> could craft them.

name: Blacksmith
description: Broad and taciturn, <name> believed [his/her] art helped forge Anglalonde, aided by the gods. 'Weland gave the Sword, The Sword gave the Treasure, and the Treasure gave the Law,' so it was said. And <name> repeated that often, to any who listened.

name: Armourer
description: <name> could bend anything to [his/her] will, especially bright metal. Formerly apprentice to a master from Chartres, <name>'s hammer and nimble fingers had worked long years in the armouries of the London arsenal. [He/She] had saved countless lives.

name: Arrowsmith
description: Tipped with blade or barbed, <name> had been turning out arrow heads since [he/she] was 14. [He/She] sometimes wondered how many of [his/her] creations had found their mark, staining the ruddy battlefields of Sluys and Crecy.

name: Barber
description: Need a close shave? When it was time to remove a troublesome beard or festering limb, <name> would merrily oblige. [He/She] loved to gossip almost as much as letting blood. <name> was often the first to know, and, for many, the last they would see.

name: Courtesan
description: <name> speaks soft and low, with a gentle laugh as pleasing as birdsong. Despite being a great storyteller, nobody knows [his/her] chequered history at court. However, <name> knows a tasty little secret about almost everyone else...

name: Alchemist
description: <name> had become disillusioned questing for the Philosopher's Stone, and sought the Elixir of Youth. [He/She] could read Greek and Arabic and made copious notes in code. <name> occasionally despaired, [his/her] dreams reduced to glittering dross.

name: Peddler
description: Traveller <name> carried needful supplies on [his/her] back like a snail, toiling between remote hamlets. The insular indwellers were always suspicious. Each time, <name> sweet-talked them into trusting [him/her], so that the bargaining could begin.

name: Tanner
description: <name> knew how to tan a hide with an animal's own brains, and with the alchemy of wood ash, excrement and festering bark. Without <name>, no one would have shoes, armour or saddles. But [he/she] was hardly popular. As jobs go, <name>'s really stank.

name: Cordwainer
description: <name> entered the Cordwainers' Guild by patrimony - 'Corio et Arte' had been [his/her] father's favourite refrain. The scent of leather revived unbidden memories of London ateliers in the shadow of St Paul's, bustling with shoemakers like <name>.

name: Journeyman armourer
description: <name> began with cuir bouilli, leather boiled in wax and sturdy enough to give a commoner some battlefield protection. Later [he/she] progressed to Brigandine armour, riveting on metal plate to shield the heart. <name> was also serviceable with a bow.

name: Cobbler
description: Hailing from <origin>, <name> liked to roam up over the downs and through the ferny holloways of England. Villagers always welcomed [him/her], as even the most humble carl or cotter had shoes for <name> to mend.

name: Miner
description: <name> had done [his/her] time in the Low Peak lead fields and the Welsh mines of the Black Prince. Pale and shunning daylight like many miners, <name> had hollow eyes and headaches. Glistening veins of gold caressed [his/her] dreams.

name: Franklin
description: Tilling lynchets into the poor, hilly soil near <origin> had been a last resort as fertile land was scarce. But <name> had done well, and won the freedom to farm their own hide. <name> felt pride, but mainly relief. [He/She] soldiered on.

name: Carter
description: <name> got sick of shoveling dung with the reeve looking over [his/her] shoulder. And sicker still of the miserable husbandman who didn't pay fair and square in ale when <name> unloaded it onto the fields. At least [he/she] had a strong back.

name: Grave digger
description: <name> dug the graves at <origin> churchyard. But it was on the bloodied field at Crécy that [he/she] did [his/her] finest work. To crack French skulls in a ditch hewn with the very same pickaxe gave <name> endless satisfaction.

name: Berner
description: <name> was top dog, the leader of the pack. [He/She] cared for the hounds, and in return these dogs were fiercely loyal. Although not of high rank, <name> commanded respect. Hounds can be ferocious when crossed.

name: Turnkey
description: Feeding, cleaning, interrogating. <name> liked the weight of keys swaying on [his/her] belt and the smell of damp straw. [He/She] was ambitious, some might say authoritarian.

name: Netmaker
description: <name> tied fragile prayers into knots of hempen twine with calloused hands. [He/She] never failed to wet the nets with a libation, in hopes of a hefty catch.

name: Recuperant
description: <name> learned patience by stitching wounds and waiting for health to return in the infirmary. [He/She] nursed a quiet resilience noticed by few.

name: Squire
description: <name> polished arms humbly, and dreamed of carrying a banner. [He/She] knew how to clean blades, take bruises, and rise early.

name: Fen scout
description: <name> knew where river mud sucked and where raiders struck. [His/Her] wyrd was written in silt and sedge.

name: Nitre miner
description: <name> made ends meet by scraping crusted saltpetre from the walls of the grotto that also served as [his/her] home. The coughing and headaches seemed a fair price to pay.

name: Quacksalver
description: <name> healed with trickery and makeshift prayer, and sometimes - just sometimes - a steady hand.

name: Brawler
description: Where laws fail, fists rule. <name> had earned coin and broken teeth brawling for bed, board and booze.

name: Infirmarian
description: <name> spent years tending the broken; scrubbing bloody flagstones, wiping seeping wounds. Neither soldier, nor sage - just a steady hand when it mattered most.

name: Quartermaster
description: <name> knew the importance of maintaining supplies since the campaign against the Scots at Neville's Cross. [He/She] could dress a wound, clothe a man, or bargain for a bucket, but had never fired a single arrow.

name: Delver
description: <name> hated the serf's life. [He/She] preferred to vanish into rock or river, emerging hours later with raw ore gleaming and the perfect story to tell.

name: Marksage
description: <name>'s bow was a puzzle, not a weapon. [He/She] sensed windrift and the curve of distance, seeing angles comrades missed. [He/She] had become a legend among archers who saw action at Calais.

name: Hermit
description: <name> had inadvertently gone from beggar to hermit, when voices [he/she] heard were deemed holy. Solitary life and food offerings from locals were both greatly beneficial in finding peace of mind.

name: Tutor
description: If <name> could instil [his/her] love of learning in [his/her] small students, it would be a reward in itself. Sadly the young Lordships were spoiled brats, who showed little promise.

name: Bear baiter
description: <name> had to keep the bear in fine fettle, but the dogs were replaceable. [He/She] stayed in the shadows and let the fur fly, once the wagers had been made.

name: Apostate
description: <name> was drawn to The Circle of Avalon. <name> had secretly despised sheepish, obedient Christians, and was relieved that others felt the same. [He/She] dreamed of Arthur’s imminent return from under the faerie hill, now that the purge was over.

name: Uprooted
description: <name> despaired. Seeing villagers die was bad, watching the <origin> sheep succumb was catastrophic. <name> did [his/her] best to ease their suffering - slitting their throats at any sign of infection. Without livestock or livelihood, <name> fled.

name: Caring
description: there was no one to tend to the animals. Hogs ran wild. Cattle starved in the winter fields. It was after <name> came upon a lifeless mare beside her newborn foal that [he/she] decided to shepherd whatever beasts were needful.

name: Cunning
description: <name> burned the putrid remains of [his/her] kin. [He/She] then followed the old grandmother deep into the forest. The cunning wicche knew every leaf, berry and fungus. <name> became fluent in the untamed language of the wild wood.

name: Rustic
description: <name> had learned to survive on foraged hedgerow fare, supplemented with the occasional stolen egg or trapped hare. <name> could make a meal from dandelion, primroses or stewed acorns. [His/Her] eyes were painful hollows, always hungry.

name: Soothsaying
description: <name> lived by the lore of oak, ash and thorn, trying to ignore the collapse of civilisation and seeking solace among the trees. [He/She] waited beneath hazel and hawthorn, listening for whispers from the fey folk. Sometimes, <name> was rewarded.

name: Spinning
description: <name> learned all about flax, for clothing, bedding, bread sacks, ropes and oil. [He/She] was soothed by retting and rolling, scutching and spinning. <name> had a steady hand, and eyes the pale, flaxen blue of a cloudless, summer sky.

name: Tireless
description: <name> got the knack of carpentry fashioning coffins for plague victims, later nailing whole families into their homes to die. Next, <name> built trebuchets in the War of Succession. Fac et aliquid operis, ut semper te diabolus inveniat occupatum!

name: Penitent
description: <name> acquired a cap marked with a red cross. It was a memento of months spent marching naked, one behind the other. Each whipped their naked, bleeding bodies with scourges spiked with nails. 'God is merciful, God is just', they wept.

name: Shrewd
description: circumstances could have been better, but [he/she] made the most of it. When <name> took to whittling amulets to ward against the Mortal Corruption, in a number of shapes to appeal to christians, jews or pagans, [he/she] got rich, fast.

name: Faithless
description: the priest beseeched <name> to repair <origin> church, despite the sickly season. [He/She] watched gloomily as the congregation gradually expired, sneezing as they broke bread together, and buried their brethren. God is dead, <name> thought.

name: Yorkist
description: <name> thought it was bleeding obvious that the royals were to blame, cutting England to the bone because of their silly French war. [He/She] had pitched in willingly to help shore up York's defenses. Someone had to make a stand.

name: Savage
description: <name> had utterly lost [his/her] mind. <name> had seen Beelzebub and there was no redemption. [He/She] could make shelter, and fire, and dream of blood and screams. <name> would not, or could not, say if [he/she] had eaten human flesh.

name: Cheerful
description: <name> would whistle as [he/she] worked, almost as though the horrors of recent times had passed [him/her] by. <name>'s reason to be cheery was simple enough. [He/She] had caught the pestilence, but had dodged the Grim Reaper. Life was good.

name: Charitable
description: <name> roved among the mills, begging or stealing flour to bake bread. This [he/she] made into simple bannocks and distributed to the starving village folk, barely clinging to the wreckage of their former lives. It kept <name> busy, and purposeful.

name: Avant-garde
description: <name> experimented. Have you tried rat au vin or eels in goat's milk? Neither had <name> until Armageddon. [He/She] was utterly fearless in combining random ingredients to keep everyone fed, leading to unexpected results and frequent indigestion.

name: Toxic
description: <name> fed a band of hungry marauders, a risky job. <name> would occasionaly cut corners to save time. Uncertain if it was a stray toadstool or mouldering rye that caused the hallucinations, <name> still maintained [he/she] did [his/her] best.

name: Clever
description: <name> believed [him/her]self spared from Mortal Sickness for a higher purpose. So said the Canterbury Friar, who taught [him/her] to read. “Knowledge is freedom”, <name> whispered softly, mounting the Friar’s mule and stealing away into the darkness.

name: Inconspicuous
description: <name> was deployed undercover to watch for heresy among royalist factions. On receiving no further instructions from [his/her] Master of Whispers, <name> sought the shadows, using what [he/she] heard to survive.

name: Ambitious
description: <name> crept about Oxford, tearing pages glowing with illuminations, swiping vellum and ink. <name> served [his/her] masters in the scriptorium dilligently. <name> had a steady hand. <name> would learn to read and write, and finally become Somebody.

name: Despicable
description: <name> took to the hills on a rampage as order crumbled. Born to privilege, <name> gathered a vile band of ruffians and killed and burned at will. [He/She] was exhilarated by chaos, amused by desecration, and not to be underestimated.

name: Accurate
description: <name> began to perform a sideshow, throwing daggers in an arc over a pretty girl for a few coins. <name> figured out [he/she] had a talent when [he/she] threw a carving knife dead into the eye of a looter. <name> never misses.

name: Confident
description: the noble's marches and forests became pretty much fair game. So <name> now poaches with impunity. [He/She] will catch what you want to order: venison, boar, rabbit, peacock. Naturally, this comes at a price.

name: Patient
description: <name> developed patience to sit in a furze bush or atop an oak tree, chewing on a blade of grass and listening to the wind. At the perfect moment, [he/she] would take down [his/her] prey with a single arrow. <name> had become an assassin.

name: Deadly
description: <name> was on a crusade to wipe out pretentious, usurping commoners and reinstate the true and righteous order of England. Blood mattered, and <name> would reclaim [his/her] birthright. The peasantry needed to be brought to their filthy knees.

name: Bloodthirsty
description: <name> recalled the healer lancing boils. Flagstones had run red as he opened veins, cursing the French, and the King. Finally <name> took the powders and purifying herbs from the dying healer's blackened hand. <name> was left holding the bloody razor.

name: Bookish
description: studying the many great works in the libraries of Oxford gave <name> confidence to try [his/her] hand at medicine. <name> was from a worthy family, the last of [his/her] name. Book learning surely surpasses base peasant cures, herbs and charms?

name: Hopeful
description: <name> fished leeches from the pond at <origin>, and carried them about in a milk jar, offering healing. <name> had no experience whatsoever, but had once seen a monk put the beasts on a dying man. It probably did no harm, <name> thought.

name: Ruthless
description: <name> recalled townsfolk dying in the streets as the nobles fled north to escape the plague. Are we not all mere sinners in the eyes of God? <name> would follow William of York in defending the rights of common folk. To the death if necessary.

name: Loyal
description: <name> pledged fealty to King Edmund, who was ordained to rule and bring England back into harmony and balance. <name> would gladly put anyone who disagreed with [him/her] to the sword. Death would be swift and merciful.

name: Chivalrous
description: <name> swooned over the histories of Sir Gawain and Sir Bedivere. To be so gallant, so merciful. <name> thought [he/she] had the right qualities to be a knight. And those qualities were sorely needed, in these savage days.

name: Weary
description: <name> was tired, truth be told. [His/Her] joints ached and [he/she] couldn't fathom how The End of Days had passed [him/her] by. <name> still oiled [his/her] blades, strangely envious of comrades slain at Saint-Omer. Somehow, <name> soldiered on.

name: Wicked
description: <name> regretted wishing death on [his/her] father's house. This very fate befell all [his/her] kin, and <name> was filled with remorse. [He/She] took up [his/her] father's hammer, and fired up the forge. Each metallic blow rang out: "Guilty, guilty."

name: Thrifty
description: <name> had left the silent streets of <origin> with a cart, and started collecting metal. From churches to manors, <name> stripped them clean and melted it all down. Sir Hugh Gaveston and William of York would surely be needing swords.

name: Tempered
description: <name> had packed [his/her] surviving children on a cart and fled. [He/She] could not remain, as the ghosts of [his/her] family would haunt the house for eternity. <name> found a niche as an ironmonger. Even the unhinged need new locks and bolts.

name: Brutal
description: <name> had fallen from grace, ending up in prison. Fate in the form of The Great Mortality - sickened guards and a filched key - offered a window of escape. <name> now had an unhealthy fascination with torture and tools of punishment.

name: Winsome
description: [he/she] became the Earl's lover. <name> had comforted him as his wife lay dying, and coerced him with blackmail when the countess unexpectedly recovered. <name> become a puppet master to the hapless Earl, his wife relegated to a distant tower.

name: Willful
description: bards told of how <name> commanded the barring of the gates, deaf to the pitiful wails and scrabbling outside. By sheer force of will, <name> kept extinction at bay in <origin>. That day, <name> became a legendary leader.

name: Artful
description: <name> chose eternal damnation over living purgatory. [He/She] sold the cow, then [his/her] only daughter. An artful beggar, [he/she] roamed the tattered shires, flattering, cajoling and seducing for a crust of bread. <name> is a survivor.

name: Crafty
description: <name> was scavenging from a bloated corpse, and came by a fine pair of shears. Trimming cloth from dead limbs was easy. Turning it into wearable garments took more practice. But <name> persisted. Now [he/she] can fashion a suit from almost anything.

name: Swindling
description: <name> raided barns for stray kittens and pups, fashioning brightly-coloured sacks from dead-men's cloaks to stash them in. Off to market! Jiggety jig. <name> would sell the unwary a pre-bagged 'piglet,' at bargain price...and vanish. Caveat emptor!

name: Thoughtless
description: <name> fancied [him/her]self a dressmaker. And so [he/she] set about using miller's floursacks, sheets and linen rags to clothe the destitute orphans and wastrels of <origin>. A frightful sight they were, shorn of their remaining dignity.

name: Reckless
description: <name> ventured into the abandoned mines, with a band of comrades and a few candle stubs. It only takes a pickaxe, any fool can do it, <name> supposed. And putting aside the fatal rockfall and the flooding incidents, <name> was right.

name: Desolate
description: <name> wanted to hit someone, to take out [his/her] rage at the horror and desolation that had violated everything [he/she] loved. But <name> was a pacifist. So [he/she] hacked spoils from the bountiful earth until [his/her] grief was spent instead.

name: Solitary
description: <name> had felt more at home in the quiet of the clay pits and lime kilns than in the towns. There were traces of humanity, but not the stench or the despair. <name> carved a secret labyrinth into the rock, invoking memories of Reims Cathedral.

name: Ashen
description: <name> had burned what could not be buried. Ash clung to [his/her] skin and throat until [he/she] forgot the scent of anything but smoke and death. It clings to [him/her] still, often in dreams.

name: Wary
description: trust was a luxury <name> could no longer afford. A smile could conceal a knife, a handhake spread a fever. [He/She] learned to remain vigilant, and to move before danger struck.

name: Tangled
description: the debts mounted quickly, and <name> tangled [himself/herself] in promises, betrayals, and desperate bargains. The plague wiped the slate clean, as there was nothing left, and nobody alive to pay.

name: Whole
description: somehow, <name> endured. Through fever, famine, and fire [he/she] remained whole - yet hollowed inside. Beneath the skin, grief festered, withering into a shape that only barely resembled [his/her] soul before.

name: Disciplined
description: with each blow and every struggle, <name> was hardened. Order became all that mattered. Without it, [he/she] believed, even the strongest crumbled into dust.

name: Gnarled
description: time twisted <name> like a winter-throttled oak. With scarred hands and a bowed back, [he/she] held fast to roots deep in the ruined earth of <origin>. Storms passed; [he/she] endured.

name: Frosty
description: <name> froze long before winter came. Each death, each burial dulled [his/her] spirit further. No comfort could thaw the frost that settled into [his/her] marrow.

name: Riven
description: the world tore <name> apart. Some pieces, [he/she] left in the mass graves; some, [he/she] buried deeper. Surely, once this harrowing was over, they had earned God's grace?

name: Seaborn
description: the sea could not weep, for it was made of tears. So, <name> raised a sail to ride [his/her] sorrow on salt and tide. Let the land rot. <name> would look to the horizon.

name: Frayed
description: hope unravelled stitch by stitch. <name> carried on anyway, patching the seams of a broken life with whatever scraps [he/she] scavenged among the ruins.

name: Candlelit
description: <name> often worked until Matins in the scriptorium at <origin> Abbey, illuminating documents by flickering tallow light. [He/She] befriended every pigment, coaxing gold leaf's gleam and verdigris to bloom. Silence was [his/her] companion, precision [his/her] obsession.

name: Merciful
description: <name> became adept with saw and iron, deftly cutting rot from living flesh. Some said [he/she] rather enjoyed it. [He/She] claimed it was an act of mercy, whispering prayers as limbs fell away.

name: Grim
description: <name> took no joy in the work, but neither did [he/she] flinch. Shackles clanked, keys turned, and bones broke where necessary. Words sometimes failed <name> - steel did not.

name: Singed
description: when sparks flew, <name> had been the first to haul buckets, drag bodies, and wrangle panicked beasts. The cleansing flames may have touched [him/her] here and there, but [he/she] was undeterred.

name: Unshaped
description: <name> had never liked drills or sparring grounds. So [he/she] was surprised to learn that when fists flew, [he/she] didn’t hesitate. <name> had finally discovered their own strength, yet knew nothing of discipline.

name: Gentle
description: <name> flinched at smoke and screaming, but never turned away from the wounded. [He/She] learned to stitch flesh, carving saints for those in [his/her] care. <name> softened the world to make the horrors more bearable.

name: Nurturing
description: <name> tended creatures and crops with quiet joy, coaxing life from egg and seed alike. Each act of care was a prayer for one of those who had perished before.

name: Studious
description: <name> practiced all arts with quiet focus, whether bladework or brushstroke. [He/She] had heard the pen was mightier than the sword, but opted to use both.

name: Lightfooted
description: <name> turned away from darkness. [He/She] had a ready smile, and would charm stories from the surliest of strangers, always chasing breeze over burden.

name: Keen
description: <name> studied tracks like an alphabet, and knew the signs to follow to avoid disturbing elves. [He/She] had witnessed many strange occurrences, but knew better than to speak of them.

name: The Red
description: The world had changed, and so had <name>. Having nothing more to lose, [he/she] joined a group of marauding bandits, and was soon their leader. Insatiable bloodlust in various assaults and squirmishes soon earned <name> a nickname 'The Red'.

name: The Butcher
description: <name> wasn’t particularly smart nor talented, so each summer, around Pentecost, [his/her] parents sent [him/her] to help Uncle Aldwin at the livestock farm. <name> proved adept at slitting throats. [He/She]’s been known as 'The Butcher' ever since.

name: The Saint
description: <name> was not averse to nursing lepers and other outcasts, but it was to the animal kingdom that [he/she] felt the deepest afinity. <name> blushed and demured when likened to St Francis, but the comparison was apt.

name: Le Chou
description: <name> spent so long in the vegetable garden as a child that [his/her] mother, of Norman stock, affectionately called [him/her] 'cabbage', as is the French way. To this day, <name> still has a green thumb, especially for brassicas.

name: The Bastard
description: An apologist for the Philosophers of the Natural Order, <name> harboured a nagging fear that wherever [his/her] errant father was, he might be a follower of Gregorius, or even a cannibal. <name>'s friends called [him/her] 'bastard' and made it worse.

name: The Pagan
description: <name> spoke to plants and buried strange parcels in the woods under the full moon. Nobody dared speak up against [him/her] due to rumours <name> could hex them. <name> did not care that other humans called [him/her] 'Pagan'. Humans were the problem.

name: The Cuckold
description: It was well known that <name>'s spouse was unfaithful, and <name> didn't seem willing or able to do anything about it. Once a beaten, unwanted child, <name> was perfectly content to gather up whatever crumbs of affection [he/she] could salvage.

name: The Rebel
description: <name> is young at heart. <name> likes to joke around and play the fool. [He/She] avoids responsibility at all costs, laughing at [his/her] elders.

name: The Apostle
description: <name> was a follower alright, and loved to go on about the scriptures. [His/Her] proselytising could become a little tiresome and repetitive. When <name> wouldn't shut up, they called [him/her] 'The Apostle'. <name> thought it was a complement.

name: The Zealot
description: <name> keeps making altars and offerings, stopping the day's business to say prayers and muttering about sin. One might be forgiven for saying [he/she] takes it a bit far.

name: The Heretic
description: <name> speaks of the God of Abraham and the mosques of the Moors, of sacred groves, lost scrolls and forbidden rites. <name> knows a bit too much for [his/her] own good.

name: The Chaste
description: <name> is pining for a dead lover, and will never marry another. <name> is living in the past, trying to stop precious memories from slipping away, and shuns all affection.

name: The Pudding
description: <name> could make an excellent fygey pudding, among other desserts. [He/She] never lacked for paramours, being bonny and sweet, with just enough spice. Lovers, rivals and jilted exes all called <name> 'pudding', with varying degrees of affection.

name: The Forlorn
description: When not complaining, <name> was weeping into [his/her] pottage. This was destinctly unappetising. It did not pay to ask <name> why [he/she] was forlorn, since [his/her] tales of woe were so distressing they would haunt your dreams forever.

name: The Tart
description: <name> was not in the least flirtatious. [He/She] got [his/her] nickname thanks to an acerbic nature, that left a bitter taste even after the briefest of interactions. <name> was the ultimate sourpuss.

name: The Doctor
description: <name> had saved a friend's life at just 10 years old, earning the title of 'doctor'. Less well known was that <name> had abandoned many beseeching patients during the unremitting horror of The Pestilence. It was a title burdened with secret shame.

name: The Fool
description: <name> had at one time played the fool at court, and revelled in being allowed to insult the high and mighty, as long as [he/she] caused enough mirth to compensate. [His/Her] cutting wit and humourous insults were unsurpassed.

name: The Spy
description: <name> had once been bribed by the abbot to listen for compromising secrets at the manor of <origin>. Alas [he/she] had been exposed and disavowed by all concerned. <name> was a pretty useless spy, but to this day, nobody trusted [him/her].

name: The Deceiver
description: As a sailor, <name> offered safe passage to desperate townsfolk attempting to flee the Tide of Death to the Western Isles or Hibernia. Once out at sea, <name> tossed them overboard, stripping their valuables. 'It's just business', <name> shrugged.

name: The Broken
description: It was said that <name>'s adventuring career came to an abrupt end when [he/she] took an arrow to the knee. [He/She] does have a funny walk.

name: The Minstrel
description: <name> had the voice of an angel and the memory of a druid. [His/Her] spellbinding tales and sweet lullabies earned <name> the honorary title of 'minstrel'.

name: The Crow
description: Some folk still left bread and milk out for the fairy folk, a custom as old as the very hills. <name> would swoop in and gobble these up, the wiley old bird.

name: The Bonesetter
description: <name> had first practiced on animals but soon moved on to human subjects. The way [he/she] hovered [his/her] hands over the damaged limb before giving a sudden, brisk wrench was almost mystical. <name> could not explain how [he/she] did it.

name: The Wakeful
description: <name> could never sleep, so [he/she] gained a reputation as a good watchman. [His/Her] night vision was highly tuned.

name: The Bold
description: <name> once took on three pirates after drinking for a day and a night. No one remembers if [he/she] prevailed through bravery or foolhardiness, but the legend lives on.

name: The Spear Maiden
description: <name> is like a fierce valkyrie from the times of the norsemen. [She] is fearless in the face of death, wild with the bloodlust of battle. They call her shieldmaiden.

name: The Confessor
description: <name> will solemnly unburden [him/her]self of a long list of [his/her] slain victims, in minute and sometimes tedious detail. Nobody really wants to hear it.

name: The Philosopher
description: <name> once read half a thing, somewhere, maybe, about turning lead into gold. Apparently urine is involved. [He/She] may be taking the piss.

name: The Lucky
description: <name> was born under a lucky horseshoe, so they said. It seemed plausible enough. Money seemed to fall in [his/her] lap, chance encounters led to romance, and the sun always shone on <name>.

name: The Prodigal
description: <name> was a quitter, [he/she] left many a task unfinished. And yet with [his/her] silver tongue, loaded with sweet flattery and plausible excuses, <name> would be welcomed back for seemingly infinite second chances.

name: The Paramour
description: Ugly as a child, <name> would never slight a lady for her looks. And in the wake of Armageddon, the value of good looks as currency was somewhat diminished. <name> helped keep spirits - and skirts - high, gaining a reputation as a satisfying lover.

name: The Riddler
description: Some people talk straight. But <name> had a way with words that certainly sounded clever, but was also a trifle confusing. Many of <name>'s pronouncements could have multiple meanings. [His/Her] friends called [him/her] The Riddler.

name: The Kitten
description: Cute, soft, endearing...<name> is certainly adorable, and people flock to [him/her] to pet [him/her]. But beware, <name> also has claws, and often leaves a trail of destruction behind [him/her].

name: The Lamb
description: <name> was docile and sweet-tempered, and so was often affectionately called lamb. Like most of [his/her] disposition, <name> had learned the hard way to be on guard against wolves.

name: The [Bridegroom/Bride]
description: <name> seemed to be forever stitching away at incredibly fine and delicate items of clothing and linens for [his/her] wedding trousseau. [He/She] became dewy eyed at the prospect of marriage. What a pity, then, that <name> had never even been kissed.

name: The Thief
description: <name> had always been nimble fingered, but became a full-time thief to survive the Dark Years. [He/She] stitched many hidden pockets into [his/her] clothes and would pinch anything that wasn't nailed down. <name> was often hired to do so.

name: The Pirate
description: <name> didn’t do much to deserve [his/her] nickname, [he/she] inherited it. <name> was from a long line of swashbucklers known for attacking and looting trading ships in the waters around British Isles. <name>, however, didn't sail, and couldn't swim.

name: The Ghost
description: <name> was pale and silent and loitered in dark alcoves. <name> seldom spoke, and often seemed to appear out of nowhere, startling people. <name> was actually a bit creepy, seeming to have more in common with the dead than the living.

name: The Hanged
description: It is told that <name> survived death by hanging. As the hangman pulled the lever and the rope jerked, <name> expected the end. But the rope suddenly snapped. As God willed it, some said, crossing themselves.

name: Vigorous
description: Bursting with health and vitality, <name> is never sick for long.

name: Robust
description: <name> appears unassailable, bouncing back swiftly from injuries that would put others in the grave.

name: Infirm
description: Fragile health is a burden that <name> has always had to bear. [He/She] is often convalescent.

name: Moribund
description: <name> often has an unwholesome smell, emanating from foetid bandages. [He/She] is slow to heal when injured.

name: Night Owl
description: <name> feels most alive working during the hours of darkness. [He/She] can survive happily with very little sleep.

name: Forty Winks
description: <name> only needs to shut [his/her] eyes for the briefest of cat naps to feel fully restored.

name: Somnolent
description: <name> loves nothing better than a nice, long snooze. In fact, [he/she] needs more sleep than most just to function.

name: Early Bird
description: <name> relishes getting to work at daybreak, when the first cock crows. An early bedtime is essential.

name: Stout
description: <name> jokes that [his/her] ample belly is a great asset, storing energy for lean times. Getting around is slower, though.

name: Gluttonous
description: Food, glorious food! <name> simply loves to eat, whenever, and wherever possible.

name: Iron Stomach
description: One of <name>'s favourite tricks is eating horseshoe nails or soap. It's a special talent to be able to eat literally anything.

name: Gourmet
description: Ah, la joie de cuisiner! <name> is everyone's favourite cook, with endless culinary skills that tantalise the tastebuds.

name: Austere
description: <name> has mastered discipline and self-denial. [He/She] often fasts, going for days without food with no ill effect.

name: Gobbler
description: The only way to preserve food is to eat it, quickly. At least that's what <name> thinks.

name: Congenial
description: Out of sight, out of mind, that's <name>'s motto. [He/She] doesn't worry about things beyond [his/her] control.

name: Outgoing
description: <name> is a great sport, always setting up bouts, games and sing alongs. [He/She] is a jolly soul.

name: Churl
description: Mean and surly, barely even civil. <name> is hard to work with and harder still to befriend.

name: Contemplative
description: <name> spends most of [his/her] time with [his/her] own thoughts. The rest of us are not invited.

name: Industrious
description: <name> is certainly a busy bee, buzzing around getting things done from dawn til dusk. [He/She] never seems to rest.

name: Lord of Misrule
description: For some, tricks and buffoonery were a midwinter indulgence, but <name> liked to play jokes all year long.

name: Hedonist
description: Without a bit of excitement, <name> quickly gets bored, and starts causing trouble. Quite the drama queen.

name: Listless
description: <name> tends to mope about complaining, and is a total wet blanket if anything fun is suggested. [He/She] generally isn't invited.

name: Benevolent
description: <name> is a ray of hope in an otherwise bleak existence. [He/She] makes everyone feel better.

name: Ruthless
description: <name> is extremely candid, and doesn't suffer fools gladly. Those who can't handle the unvarnished truth tend to steer clear.

name: Brawler
description: Whenever a fist fight breaks out, you can guarantee that <name> started it.

name: Disfigured
description: After the fire, <name> did not really have a face, but [he/she] had a purpose. Few will look <name> in the eye.

name: Ill-favoured
description: <name> was born with a boss eye, which made it difficult to know where to look when speaking to [him/her].

name: Winsome
description: Everyone loved <name>: the shy and the bold, knights, children, young and old. [He/She] was beautiful to behold.

name: Fair
description: Who is the fairest of them all? <name> of course! [His/Her] natural charm makes it very hard for anyone to say 'no'.

name: Ravishing
description: Of all the flowers in <village_name>, <name> bearest the prize. [He/She] is as bonny and blithe as a summer breeze.

name: Swigger
description: It's thirsty work! <name> likes to drink on the job, and it makes [him/her] work faster.

name: Punch Drunk
description: If you share alcohol with <name>, expect a black eye, or worse. [He/She] is an angry drunk.

name: Lightweight
description: <name> really cannot hold [his/her] drink. Even a tiny tipple will make <name> doze off.

name: Heat resistant
description: Even in scorching conditions, <name> can take the heat. [He/She] loves working in the sun.

name: Cold hardy
description: <name> seems impervious to the cold. [He/She] works on throughout the harshest days of winter.

name: Hot-blooded
description: <name> seems to be permanently overheated, throwing open windows and shunning warm clothes. [He/She] should be kept cool.

name: Chilly
description: <name> always complains of draughts and chills, and huddles close to the fire. [He/She] must be kept warm.

name: Vulnerable
description: <name> suffers constantly from gout or flux, rashes or spasms. [His/Her] constitution is decidedly feeble.

name: Elf Shot
description: Excruciating back pains that <name> endures were doubtless caused by fairy arrows. What had [he/she] done to deserve such misery?

name: Green Thumb
description: <name> has always loved plants...sometimes better than people. [He/She] tends them, and they thrive.

name: Strapping
description: <name> is as strong as an ox. [He/She] is always hale and hearty, and never laid low.

name: Wicche
description: <name> is highly attuned to the natural world. [He/She] listens closely to the feral whispers of plants and animals.

name: Ascetic
description: <name> has mastered discipline and self-denial. [He/She] shuns comfort, preferring the austerity of a cold, bare cell.

name: Dainty
description: <name> needs the finer things in life to thrive. [He/She] struggles to cope with little things like dirt, cold and hardship.

name: Precious
description: <name> is thin skinned, delicate and nervy. It is important to keep [him/her] comfortable.

name: Whirlwind
description: <name> runs like the wind, fleet as a deer. [He/She] also walks at quite a clip.

name: Fleet Footed
description: It always feels as though <name> is one step ahead. [His/Her] long legs and rapid stride are the reason.

name: Brawny
description: <name> is powerful and carries out tough jobs effortlessly.

name: Sluggardly
description: Always tardy, always tired. <name> is short on punctuality and is slow to get things done.

name: Laggardly
description: <name> struggles to keep up. [He/She] lags behind the others, and takes longer than most to perform the smallest task.

name: Hefty
description: <name> is exceptionally large, practically a giant in fact. [He/She] is not built for speed.

name: Sun Seeker
description: <name> comes alive when the sun is shining. A few golden rays is all it takes to bring out the best in [him/her].

name: Snow White
description: <name> loves nothing better than the biting air and crisp frost of midwinter. [He/She] thrives in the cold.

name: Washout
description: If there are rainclouds about, <name> is going to be very unhappy. Getting wet makes [him/her] as miserable as sin.

name: Dullard
description: It takes <name> a long time to catch on to things, and [he/she] requires a lot of patience. Even then, <name> may not understand.

name: Wise
description: <name> often sees things from a new angle, and thinks differently from most. [He/She] is a problem solver.

name: Erudite
description: <name> has a rare intellect, and could even be called gifted. [He/She] learns extremely quickly.

name: Bloodlust
description: <name> comes into [his/her] own in a fight, roused by the prospect of violent slaughter.

name: Callous
description: <name> is unmoved by human mortality. Flesh is a mere commodity, once the soul has fled.

name: Cannibal
description: <name> is a merciless butcher and devourer of men. [He/She] is fortified by human flesh.
